chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a garment in which a man becomes junub and sweats in it. He said: As for me, I do not like to sleep in it; and if it is winter, then there is no problem so long as he has not sweated in it.
So the import of this report is a kind of dislike, and it is explicit in that; and it is possible that it is to be understood as referring to when the janābah is from what is haram.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّ: an expression indicating dislike or karāhah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or objection
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: to enter the state of janābah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing or sleeping in a garment in which one became junub and perspired?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on a garment in which a person entered the state of janābah and perspired. Its apparent meaning indicates karāhah, especially regarding sleeping in such a garment, while allowing leniency in winter if no sweating occurred; it may also be understood in connection with janābah arising from haram.
